title: The 'jazz symphony' Jubilee broadcast
summary: He was unaware the rehearsal was a live broadcast; four pieces were billed as a symphony.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I may be too unkind, that may not be typical,--that may not be universal, but it's typical. Anyway, let me get back to this. "Barefoot Boyd" I think it was "--With Cheek"
All four of them are there?
No, only three. The fourth one is--"Dalvatore" is not on this V disc.
I don't know whose idea it was to call those four separate pieces of music a symphony, first movement, second movement, because that's not true at all.
You were there and allowed it.
It happened in front of my face on the air; could I possibly stop it? No way in hell.
That was the first time it had ever been presented that way?

As a matter of fact, that whole scene was ridiculous, the way it happened. I was coming to rehearse a chart that I had written, I was not told that there was going to be a performance, that we were actually giving

a concert on the air, live, with an audience. I showed up in a torn shirt, dirty jeans, haraches on my feet, no socks, unshaven; I was coming to a rehearsal. That's all I was told. I get there and I walked in and there's a thousand people sitting out there in front, everything going on.
Where was that?
In Hollywood. CBS--one of the big studios.

I couldn't believe it. I said, what the hell is going on. We're going on the air in ten minutes, here's what you do; this guy's going to introduce you. Man, why didn't you tell me about this, why did you let me come like this. That's how that happened.

I didn't even know that I was supposed to talk with this guy, the M.C., because after it was over, I walked off and he's supposed to be carrying on a conversation with me and I'm not even there; I didn't have a script, I didn't know what was happening. I left; finished the last piece of music and walked off and he's saying
yeah, that's very good, George, what about the-- and I'm not there, so he had to ad lib himself out of it.
That's what happened that day.
There was a series of records of that Jubilee Show and he's on all of them. A very noisy man.
A real fool. He's somebody you would recognize.
I'm sure.
He's been in a lot of movies. I see him on all the shows that I see. The typical big, heavy spade actor. Jazz symphony--never written a jazz symphony.
